subject: Acme Renewal & Expansion - Usage Review + Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Renewal & Expansion - Usage Review + Next Steps

Thanks again for taking the call today - great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we discussed and the proposed next steps so we're all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of current state
- Current contract renewal date: 2026-09-30 (Q4).
- Avg monthly token usage: ~3.1B tokens (up 35% YoY); peak concurrency causing occasional tail latency for real-time features.
- Current plan: Hosted API with burst capacity; no dedicated pools.

Primary pain points
1) Latency spikes during peak hours impacting user experience for real-time chat.
2) Rising per-token costs as usage grows - need predictable unit economics.
3) Internal security/compliance checks for audit logs and longer retention for debug traces.

Goals identified
- Reduce 99th-percentile latency by ~30-40% during peak windows.
- Move to a pricing model that gives cost predictability for Q4+2027.
- Support two new workloads: (a) high-concurrency chat (real-time), (b) nightly batch embeddings for search.

Recommended expansion path (high level)
- Short-term (Q4): Reserve a dedicated pool sized for peak concurrency to hit latency SLOs.
- Medium-term: Adopt Redwood Dedicated with autoscale buffer and prefix caching for nightly batch jobs; enable KV-cache to lower token usage for prompt-heavy sessions.
- Optional: Consider 4-bit quantized model variant for batch embeddings to reduce unit cost on search workload.

Pricing / timeline
- I will share an updated renewal + expansion pricing workbook (attached) with a proposal that combines a 12-month renewal + reserved capacity commitment (sized to current 1.5x peak).
- Your team indicated an internal procurement deadline of ~2026-09-20.

Action items / next steps
1) Marissa: Send updated pricing workbook and usage dashboard (attached) - by EOD Monday 2026-08-16.
2) Samantha/Tom: Confirm decision makers that need to be looped (legal/procurement) and confirm procurement timeline.
3) Schedule follow-up: 60-min renewal + technical planning call week of 2026-08-24 to review sizing and SLA.

Attachments: Acme_usage_dashboard_Jul2026.pdf, ACME_updated_renewal_pricing_v2.xlsx

Thanks - looking forward to getting this over the finish line.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0162
Redwood Inference — inference that scales

Hi Marissa - thanks for the recap and for sending the dashboard. This is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The latency spikes are most visible between 1pm-3pm PT when our consumer traffic surges. A 30% reduction in p99 would be a big win.
- For procurement, Legal will need a copy of the audit log retention policy and SOC 2 scope (can you share those assets?).
- Decision makers to include: myself, Tom Reyes (Head of Engineering), and Procurement (cc'd). We may also loop in our CTO if we land on a Dedicated commitment.

We reviewed the proposed timeline internally and can target the week of 2026-09-20 for a final procurement sign-off; however, we want to make progress on sizing earlier. The week of 2026-08-24 for a technical planning call works for Tom and me - Wed 08/26 10:00am PT or Thu 08/27 9:00am PT are both possible.

Please also include a short note in the pricing workbook that outlines the rollback/fallback plan (if we need to step down from Dedicated to Hosted).

On attachments: I'm attaching a small usage extract that shows peak windows (see attached "acme_peak_extract_Aug2026.csv").

Thanks,
Samantha
